text:
anna: Quick check — after yesterday's runtime patch (v1.12.3) we're seeing a ~6% drop in KV prefix-cache hit rate on ded10 during long-prefix traffic. Can someone run a focused microbench on the ded10 pool (seq len distribution skewed to long prefixes) and share eviction/hit histograms? I pushed a tiny script: infra/bench/kv_slot_align.py and a sample config in infra/bench/configs/long_prefix.yaml

mike: On it. will kick off a run now with seq_len=[64,128,512], batch=16. pinging @rajiv for shard-pset alignment info — there was a recent rebalance right?

rajiv: Yep, we had a passive rebalance on ded10 yesterday morning to spread hot prefixes. I can run a targeted job that isolates the 3 affected shards (shard ids: 42,43,44). Need the exact traffic mix — can you paste the perf counters you observed?

anna: counters from canary window (paste below):
```
evictions/sec: 0.27
kv_hits: 84231
kv_misses: 15623
hit_rate: 0.843
avg_kv_latency_ms: 1.9
cache_frag_percent: 18.4
```
Also saw a small uptick in prefix fragmentation in the heatmap (attached) — higher occupancy variance on slots 12-15.

bench-bot: Benchmark job queued: job_id=4623 target_pool=ded10 shards=[42,43,44] config=long_prefix.yaml

sarah: Quick thought — did the eviction_threshold param flip in the runtime config? I remember a revert candidate was proposed but might've been shipped to canary. Even a small threshold change can shift compression/alignment.

rajiv: Good call. I checked: config diff shows eviction_threshold from 0.6 -> 0.7 during the patch. I'll revert that in canary and re-run the microbench before touching prod.

mike: Running the baseline now (job 4623). Will run A: current canary, B: canary+eviction_threshold_revert, C: previous stable. I'll snapshot eviction histograms and per-slot occupancy.

(30m later)
rajiv: Quick results summary from the targeted runs:
```
A (canary, eviction_threshold=0.7): hit_rate=0.842, cache_frag=18.7, evictions/sec=0.28
B (revert -> 0.6): hit_rate=0.915, cache_frag=12.1, evictions/sec=0.09
C (stable): hit_rate=0.918, cache_frag=11.8, evictions/sec=0.08
```
Reverting the threshold recovers most of the hit rate. Looks like the higher threshold increases premature evictions for long prefixes due to slot misalignment.

anna: That's really helpful, thanks. Can you include the per-slot histograms? I want to check if slots 12-15 still have high variance after revert.

rajiv: Uploaded histograms to the job artifacts (link: https://artifacts/redwood/4623/histograms.tar.gz). Slots 12-15 went from var=0.62 -> 0.21 after revert.

mike: Created a tiny PR to pin eviction_threshold=0.6 for ded10 and added a rollout note: https://git.internal/repo/runtime/PR-3456 — includes bench logs and artifact links.

sarah: Nice. Can we also add a short perf test to CI that runs a 5m long-prefix scenario so we catch this regression earlier?

anna: Yes please. @mike can you add the CI job (fast smoke bench) + a perf alert if hit_rate drops >3% vs baseline?

mike: Yep will add a short job to the nightly perf pipeline and a Grafana alert (team-runtime/perf-kv-hit-rate).

anna: OK, plan: 1) revert to eviction_threshold=0.6 on ded10 (PR merged), 2) add CI smoke-job + alert, 3) follow-up retro item to review rebalance heuristics for long-prefix workloads. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

bench-bot: job 4623 completed. artifacts: https://artifacts/redwood/4623/

rajiv: PR merged and canary reverted. Will watch the canary window for next 2h and report if anything else pops.

mike: CI smoke job added as nightly.short_kv_long_prefix, alert created.

anna: Closing this thread. Adding retro card.

sarah: Adding notes to the rollout doc + tagging infra. :eyes:
